- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underreacts to sharp price spikes in history; fails to anticipate or amplify sudden increases.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — forecasts often revert too quickly to historical lows, ignoring recent momentum.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent price movements; especially in the first 5–7 days, model is too slow to catch up.
- Overshoots occur after spikes — model predicts a peak and then drops too aggressively, missing the true continuation or plateau.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast, especially when history shows volatility or recovery.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture abrupt changes or sudden reversals in price direction.
- Model underweights recent history when forecasting; over-reliance on older data leads to underestimation of short-term volatility.
- Forecasts often underestimate the true magnitude of price increases during periods of policy or market intervention.
